cards.title: B-366: Falcon 2 OBJ and in-game barrel stretch
cards.description: Mike reported that Falcon 2 loads with the end of the barrel stretched/skewed and the extracted OBJ has the same bad shape, then asked to check all weapons for a model extraction process issue. He later confirmed the in-game stretch persisted with the tip staying fixed while the model moved.
cards.notes: Code/build/smoke verified 2026-05-22; pending Mike's visual retest of Falcon 2 in-game and its extracted OBJ before closure. Extracted OBJ root cause was .pdmesh OBJ export ignoring G_MTX/G_POPMTX modelview commands and the SPSEGMENT_MODEL_MTX table used by weapon display lists, so local unposed weapon parts could be written into OBJ data and then embedded into .pdweapon archives. The exporter now builds default model matrices from model position nodes, applies the matrix stack while emitting OBJ vertices, writes model_obj_mtx_v8/export_version.txt metadata, and bumps .pdmesh plus .pdweapon cache markers through embedded.v9 / pdweapon_embedded_v9 so stale standalone and nested held meshes rebuild. Remaining in-game root cause matched Mike's tip-fixed-while-model-moved clue: the Falcon laser beam far endpoint was projected from the crosshair while the near endpoint followed the muzzle/root. bgunUpdateLasersight now derives both near and far endpoints from the muzzle matrix/local forward vector before projection, while the steady-state gate keeps stale equip/busy beams hidden. cards.title: B-323 post-boot AV in challengesInit (Pass C side-effect, N64-vs-PC stride)
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 (competent-saha-a202bb). Mike's playtest of dev 1363ee75 AVs at boot inside challengesInit() -- bcopy/memcpy+146 from a dmaExecWithAutoAlign over-read in src/game/challenge.c::challengeLoadConfig. Root cause: PC sizeof(struct mpconfig) = 4596 and sizeof(struct mpstrings) = 680 used as both stride and read length, but on-disk segment is laid out with N64 sizes (mpstrings 320 bytes/entry); MAX_BOTS grew 8 -> 32. Pre-Pass-C the over-read landed in adjacent ROM bytes inside the contiguous 32 MB g_RomFile -- harmless. Post-Pass-C (S607, dev b15cc701) each segment is its own heap allocation; over-read AVs. g_MpChallenges[0].confignum=14 makes the very first call attempt a 4596-byte read at offset 14*4596=64344, ~60 KB past the 4576-byte segment. Fix: (1) Remove mpconfigs dmaExec entirely (data was always overwritten by mpconfig->config = g_MpConfigs[confignum] -- dead code). (2) Replace mpstrings dmaExec with bcopy of N64_MPSTRINGS_SIZE=320 bytes from confignum*320, into the head of the PC mpstrings struct (description[200] + aibotnames[0..7] = 320 bytes matches N64 layout exactly), with bzero of the whole PC struct first to leave aibotnames[8..31] zeroed. Bots 9..32 fall back to legacy g_BotConfigsArray naming. Build verify clean four-target via build-session.ps1 -Session b323: client 55.5 MB, updater 12.3 MB, server 22.4 MB, tests 24.6 MB. Audit append in context/audits/catalog-universality-pivot-plan-2026-05-02.md 'BYOR post-boot AV triaged' section. Bug ledger entry at B-323. Note: NOT a BYOR-completion issue -- this AV exists in BOTH pre-BYOR and post-BYOR builds; the user's prompt framing was inaccurate.

cards.title: B-324 / B-325 / B-326 walker-after-emitters reorder + Dev Window ROM placement
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 (gifted-bohr-62309b). Three-bug coherent ship from Mike's playtest 2026-05-03 20:40 ET on dev 232d05ea (BYOR completion + Phase 3 + B-323 build). B-324 (CRITICAL): bgunCalculateBlend AV at bondgun.c:3526 dereferencing NULL weapon returned by weaponFindById(0). Stack via addr2line: bgunCalculateBlend -> bgunReset (bondgunreset.c:231) -> lvReset (lv.c:618) -> mainLoop -> mainProc -> main. cards.title: Dev Window Clear Worktrees button (replaces Prune)
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-11 (flamboyant-ride-cc996f). Mike's report: existing build-tool button doesn't actually clear worktrees. Diagnosis: BtnPruneWorktrees ran only `git worktree prune -v`, which clears stale registry entries (registry-pointing-at-deleted-dir) but never removes on-disk worktrees or their branches. With 18 worktrees on disk + 27 prunable registry entries at session start, a click cleared the 27 ghost entries and left the 18 active dirs untouched. Fix: full clear flow with disk-space accounting in devtools/dev-window-v2/dev-window-v2.ps1. Button label/content -> 'Clear Worktrees...'. On click: enumerate .claude/worktrees/ via async runspace (git worktree list --porcelain joined with on-disk Get-ChildItem), compute per-dir recursive size via DirectoryInfo.EnumerateFiles, skip reparse points to avoid junction loops. Modal WPF dialog (Show-WorktreeClearDialog) with DataGrid: checkbox + Name + Branch + Last Modified + Size, header showing on-disk count + total size + stale-prunable count, an 'Also prune N stale registry entries' checkbox (default ON when N>0), Select All / Select None / Cancel / Clear Selected buttons, live 'Selected: K worktrees, B' summary that updates on each cell edit. Skips the currently-active worktree. Worker scriptblock ($script:WorktreeClearWorker): for each selected entry, try `git worktree remove <path>`, fall back to `git worktree remove --force <path>` on dirty/untracked failure, then fall back to Remove-Item -Recurse -Force if the dir still exists. After removal, probe `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>` and run `git branch -D <branch>` if the branch still exists (worktree remove does not delete branches). Optional `git worktree prune -v` after the per-entry loop. Returns per-row report with size before, freed bytes, and step trace; UI logs each step in the Log tab and pops a Done dialog with totals. INPC row model (PD2V2.WorktreeEntry) added to the consolidated Add-Type block so DataGridCheckBoxColumn two-way binding works correctly with Select All / Select None refreshes. End-to-end verification on real worktree set: synthetic test worktree (1.04 GB on disk, branch test/wt-clear-test-*) created, enumerated, cleared via the same worker logic the GUI button drives -- worktree dir gone, branch deleted, prune ran exit 0. PowerShell bug fixed during verify: inside an `@(...)` array literal, `"refs/heads/" + $branch` was being parsed as TWO elements (string + unary-+ var) because comma binds tighter than +; parenthesised the concat to force binary-+ inside the element. Same bug would have existed in the GUI button's worker -- both call sites fixed. Scripts-only change; no C/C++ touched. .claude/scratch/ added to .gitignore. Test script at .claude/scratch/test-worktree-clear-e2e.ps1 (untracked, kept for future regression checks).

cards.title: Kanban server self-start + auto-exit on tab close
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-11 (worktree peaceful-babbage-26b748). Kanban server now ephemeral: spawned by Dev Window v2 button (c117) and self-terminates when no tab is heartbeating. Page POSTs /heartbeat every 5s; on beforeunload sends navigator.sendBeacon('/shutdown-now', ...). Server tracks _last_heartbeat_at under a lock and runs a daemon watcher thread (2s interval) that calls server.shutdown() once idle exceeds KANBAN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S (default 15). Startup grace: _last_heartbeat_at = time.time() + STARTUP_GRACE_S (default 30) so a slow browser launch is not a problem. /shutdown-now is cooperative: backdates the clock to fire SHUTDOWN_NOW_GRACE_S (default 6) seconds later, but any heartbeat from another tab resets it so multi-tab close-one keeps the server alive. /shutdown-now is idempotent. Env vars KANBAN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S, KANBAN_STARTUP_GRACE_S, KANBAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S override defaults. Verified all 5 scenarios (cold-to-close, idle-no-beacon, multi-tab survives, launch-no-connect, manual launch smoke) via .claude/scratch/probe-ephemeral-kanban.py (gitignored). cards.title: B-350: airborne side-entry through overhead collision blockers
cards.description: Track the 2026-05-19 physics-collision slice even though it was started and completed in one session. Mike's CI Training playtest showed c038/B-339 improved top/bottom jump collision, but the player could still jump sideways through overhead solid blockers and could get stuck above a doorway or inside a new blocker. Dynamic couch collision looked correct after moving the couch.
cards.notes:
Code/build slice completed 2026-05-19. Root cause: player airborne movement applied horizontal X/Z first, then bwalkUpdateVertical() only swept move=(0, verticalDelta, 0), so side-entry during a jump could bypass the side plane before vertical clamping. Fix: src/game/bondwalk.c adds bwalkClampAirborneSideEntry(), an upward diagonal capsuleSweep() from bondprevpos to the already-applied X/Z plus verticalDelta; on hit it rolls X/Z back to the safe fraction and clamps/kills upward velocity for ceiling-class hits. Test fixture now covers side-wall rendered triangles. Verification passed: scoped git diff --check, b350side tests target, focused [physics][jump] (99 assertions / 4 cases), and b350side all-target build. Manual CI Training retest remains the closure gate.
2026-05-22 B-367 follow-up: Mike reported the jumping player still clips into walls, ceilings, or corners. Root cause was the remaining horizontal half of the movement-order split: apex/descent lateral motion still committed through the legacy cylinder path before any capsule mesh repair ran. Fix: bwalkClampAirborneLateralEntry() now runs immediately after horizontal movement and before speed correction when airborne, uses the collision-owned capsule mesh sweep from bondprevpos, rolls X/Z back on wall/ceiling/corner hits, and ignores floor-class hits. Verification passed: focused [physics][jump] (105 assertions / 4 cases) and jump367 all-target build. Manual retest remains the closure gate.
Priority pass 2026-05-20: Collision critical path. Manual CI Training retest remains the gate before broader gameplay-stability work is treated as reliable.

cards.description: Follow-up from Mike's question: when updater cleanup removes stale install-root files or folders, user-visible payload cleanup should send items to the Windows Recycle Bin instead of permanently deleting them.

cards.title: Asset Pipeline: clean self-contained archive layouts
cards.description: Define the clean self-contained format for every typed or otherwise referenceable asset family first, then rebuild extraction/examples/validators to match those frozen contracts. Human-authored files stay obvious at archive root or in purpose-named folders; machine/provenance/validation data moves under _meta/. Every archive remains fully self-contained: all descriptor, source-format, material, graph, nested-descriptor, and payload references must resolve inside the archive or inside an embedded typed archive. .pdmod remains transport only.
cards.notes: Created 2026-05-21 from Mike's request to walk each asset type and implement the clean-but-functional archive shape. Reprioritized 2026-05-22 as the top Asset Pipeline migration plan. Process order is locked: first define every asset-family format, starting with c3832 for .pdweapon; then freeze the contracts; then rebuild extraction/examples/validators in the full sweep. Shared contract: root descriptor required; no .pdwpn; no authored .bin; no reference-only dependency closure; duplicate embedded payloads are allowed on disk and deduped after ingestion by catalog identity and canonical SHA-256. Preferred archive zones are authoring files first, nested typed dependencies second, and _meta/ for manifest.json, inventory.json, provenance.json, validation reports, source handles, SHA rows, and compatibility bookkeeping. During transition, scanners/loaders may accept old root manifest.json and root SHA sidecars but new emitters should write _meta/ and release validation should fail stale installed outputs that are non-zip, .pdwpn, .bin-backed, descriptor-less, or unresolved internally. c3832 is the detailed .pdweapon format card and sits immediately under this migration plan. Approved 2026-05-23 first format decisions: .pdweapon, .pdprojectile, .pdentity, .pdmaterial, and .pdtexture are recorded on this single tracker. Higher-level assets link typed dependencies by catalog ID and self-contained exports embed those dependency assets as intact typed archives under dependencies/assets; they do not absorb dependency internals into the parent schema. Approved 2026-05-23 second format batch: .pdcharacter, .pdhead, .pdbody, .pdarena, and .pdscenario are recorded on this single tracker. Character is an assembler/meta asset; body owns skeleton and first-person hands; head owns head-specific rig/expression data; arena wraps playable multiplayer selection metadata around an embedded scenario; scenario owns level content and spawn profiles for default, gametype/team, CTF/objective, and mission-phase respawn cases. Approved 2026-05-23 third format batch: .pdmesh, .pdanim, .pdsfx, .pdvoice, and .pdsong are recorded on this single tracker. Mesh owns reusable geometry and rig-facing model data; animation owns reusable timelines/events/retargeting metadata; SFX owns atomic sound sources and playback metadata; voice owns spoken-line metadata, per-locale audio variants, subtitle bindings, voice-mod override compatibility, and global-language fallback behavior while .pdlang owns text strings; song owns editable sequence/track music data and adaptive playback metadata. Continue family prompts after .pdsong.
